content.title: Liverpool vs PSG Lineups, Injuries, Live Streaming, Cable, How & Where to Watch
content.text: Liverpool welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Anfield for the decisive second leg of their Champions League quarter-final clash.Apr 14, 2026 10:00 AM EDTVirgil van Dijk of Liverpool (R) and Hugo Ekitike of Liverpool look on during the Premier League match between Manchester City and LiverpoolPhoto by Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images Liverpool host Paris Saint-Germain at Anfield as the Reds look to overcome a 2-0 deficit to secure their place in the Champions League semi-final. Arne Slot’s side enters the match following an encouraging domestic victory over Fulham. Goals from Rio Ngumoha and Mohamed Salah in that fixture ensured the club remained in fifth place in the Premier League standings. Despite the pressure, Slot has expressed full confidence in his squad, maintaining that the team is capable of delivering a historic performance in front of their home supporters. “Yes, there is a belief we can do special things but we also need to be very, very, very special because we are playing against the champions of Europe, so that makes the task more complicated but not impossible,” he said. Arne Slot, Manager of Liverpool, looks on prior to the Premier League match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Liverpool.Photo by David Rogers/Getty Images Meanwhile, PSG have had a period of rest, having not played a competitive fixture since the opening leg. Historical records might also favor the visitors. Liverpool have progressed only twice, in 1991 and 2019, when trying to overturn a deficit of two goals or more after losing the first leg away from home. Liverpool vs PSG Official Lineups and Injuries Liverpool remains without the services of Alisson Becker, Wataru Endo, Giovanni Leoni, and Conor Bradley. However, Curtis Jones is expected to be available for selection despite an injury scare against Fulham. As for Paris Saint-Germain, Fabian Ruiz is ruled out with a knee injury, but Bradley Barcola could make his return to the squad after recovering from an ankle issue. Liverpool: Goalkeeper: Mamardashvili Defenders: Frimpong, Konaté, Van Dijk, Kerkez Midfielders: Gravenberch, Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz Forwards: Isak, Ekitike PSG: Goalkeeper: Safonov Defenders: Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, N. Mendes Midfielders: Vitinha, J. Neves, Zaïre-Emery Forward: Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé, Doué The Liverpool vs. PSG UEFA Champions League quarterfinal second leg will kick off at 3:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, April 14, 2026. US viewers can watch it live on Paramount+, with coverage also available for Spanish fans on ViX, UNIMÁS, or TUDN.
